newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan denies South Africa stowaways charge.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan denies South Africa stowaways charge.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday denied South African reports that a Taiwanese trawler had put 12 Nigerian stowaways overboard in mid-ocean, saying it had been confused with a Thai vessel.
Foreign ministry deputy spokesman Chen Yung-tso told reporters Taiwan had asked its embassy in South Africa to make checks and it had come back saying the vessel was Thai.
"It is a mistake. The ship was a Thai cargo vessel with a Thai captain," Chen said. "We have asked South African radio to clarify the error that they made," he added.
Eleven Nigerian stowaways who washed up on an island off the South African coast were reported on Wednesday to have claimed they were put overboard at sea by a Taiwanese trawler.
They said a 12th man had drowned after they were forced off the ship with oil drums to keep them afloat about three days earlier, a South African nature conservation spokesman said.

They washed up on Tuesday night on Dyer Island, off the southernmost tip of the continent at Cape Agulhas. The island, which has important sea bird colonies, is permanently staffed by conservation officials.
